description: Statistics of the channels of a polyphonic cable — mean, median, mode and six more — each on its own jack

params.text: Alt mode: recalculates every sample rather than every 10ms, at a heavy cost in CPU

inputs.text: The channels the statistics are calculated from

outputs.text: The input channels added together and divided by how many there are
The middle value of the input channels once sorted, or the average of the middle two when the count is even
Every value that occurs more than once and as often as any other, one per channel; values must match exactly, and with no repeats this jack carries no channels
All the input channels multiplied together, then the nth root of that taken, where n is the channel count; one channel at 0V makes the result 0V
All the input channels multiplied together, which reaches millions of volts from ordinary inputs
How many channels the input carries, at a volt each, so sixteen channels give 16V
The input channels added together, which passes 10V readily
The input channels sorted from lowest to highest, one per channel, despite the panel printing Sort
The input channels with duplicates dropped, two values counting as the same when they are within 0.001V of each other; the manual gives this tolerance as 0.0001V

notes: nothing is calculated until a cable is patched into the input, and the outputs hold whatever they last carried.
